The range of $\theta =\operatorname{arctan}⁡x$ is given by

$$
-{90}^{∘}<\theta <{90}^{∘}.
$$

Note that the angle $\theta $ spans the first and fourth quadrants.

Since $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ is positive, our answer is an angle that lies in the first quadrant, where tangent is positive.

From the special values of the trigonometric functions, we know that 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡{30}^{∘}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}.
$$

Since ${30}^{∘}$ is an angle in the first quadrant that lies within the range of $arctan,$ we conclude that

$$
\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}})={30}^{∘}.
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}) & =3\cdot ({30}^{∘}) \\  & ={90}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
